findings.title: `firstName` returns undefined for single-word names
findings.body: The function `firstName` uses `split(' ')[1]`, which returns `undefined` when the input has only one word. For example, `firstName('Ada')` returns `undefined`, causing `welcomeBack('Ada')` to return "Welcome back, undefined!". This is wrong behavior users will hit.

evidence.expected: a first name, or an error for single-word input

findings.suggestion: Handle single-word names: return the whole name if there's no space, or throw an error.

findings.title: `welcomeBack` propagates undefined from `firstName`
findings.body: When `firstName` returns undefined, `welcomeBack` concatenates it into the greeting, producing "Welcome back, undefined!"

evidence.expected: a greeting with a proper name

findings.title: Test assertion is too loose to catch the bug
findings.body: The test only checks that the output starts with "Welcome back, " but doesn't verify the actual first name. A regex like `/^Welcome back, /` passes even when the name is undefined.

evidence.actual: The test passes because the regex only checks the prefix

findings.suggestion: Use `expect(welcomeBack('Ada Lovelace')).toBe('Welcome back, Lovelace!')` for an exact match.
